author: Bobby Grayson
description: The readiness metric taught something: aggregate blocker counts fell by half while the translated count did not move, because translation is all-or-nothing per module. The right round-8 target is the per-module tail, driven by the 'closest to translatable' list (LogStore distance 0, then four modules at distance 1), not by the frequency table. LogStore is one fix away: unify reply types across {:reply, r, _} shapes instead of falling back to opaque term().
title: Round 7 outcome: blockers 1621 -> 848 across the five real projects (loom 767->326, ensemble 749->454), but translatable is still 1/55 because each remaining module is blocked by its OWN single distinct translator error, not a shared family. Distinct failure reasons are nearly all unique: reply-type inference too weak (Ensemble.LogStore: distance 0, zero blocker families, fails only on 'reply entries has type List Term but reply inferred as opaque term()'), message tag at two arities, init not ending in {:ok, state}, tuple message patterns, field access on a struct chain
